On 2026-11-20 the user asked to "work on a1+ Unit 7 same all deal as before none stop all approved": the A1+ Unit 7 map (A1+ 7.Y follows A1 7.Y, one step each, fifteen lessons) approved up front, straight to Preview, Gemini 2.5 Flash photos and ElevenLabs audio pre-approved, no per-lesson gates, reviewed in Preview. Three new photos (Gemini 2.5 Flash): Sofia, Ana and Luis against a wall from shortest to tallest, Diego with a big black, a medium brown and a tiny white dog, and a big green, a medium white and a small red house. Every wrong option is false of its photo; the other true sentences about the same photo are never offered as wrong.

lesson.title: 7.11 Luis is the tallest
lesson.unit_title: Everyday needs, plans and free time
lesson.unit_outcome: Say what hurts and why someone feels a certain way, describe what people are wearing and the weather as it happens, tell someone to put on or take off clothes, talk about what people like doing, invite and answer, ask someone to repeat or explain, talk about being sick, the months and seasons, compare with the biggest and the tallest, and say what people and animals can do and are good at.
lesson.goal: Compare three people or things with the + -est (Luis is the tallest. / The red house is the smallest.) and ask Which … is the biggest?.
lesson.grammar_function: A follow-up of A1 7.11 Outdoors, where A1 names the things around us; A1+ 7.11 compares three of them. The one new grammar relationship is the + adjective + -est for the top of three (Luis is the tallest. / The black dog is the biggest.), set against A1+ 2.11's -er than for two (Luis is taller than Sofia.); big doubles its g (bigger, biggest). Three new photos line up three of a kind: Sofia, Ana and Luis by height, Diego's three dogs and three houses on a street; A1+ 2.10's The red one. answers Which …?.
lesson.prerequisite: A1+ 2.10 Which one? The red one.; A1+ 2.11 -er than; A1 2.11 big and small; A1 1.10 dog; A1 4.15 house.
lesson.speaking_outcome: Say the -est ending clearly (TALL-ist, BIG-ist, SMALL-ist) and stress the adjective. Do not require native-like speed.
